title: SPY 200-day trend
description: Buy SPY when it closes above its 200-day average, sell when it falls back below, 5 bps costs.
strategy:
name: SPY 200-day trend
universe: SPY
costs: 5 bps

buy when close > sma(200)
sell when close < sma(200)

title: 60/40 with trend filters
description: Hold 60% SPY and 40% TLT from 2010, rebalanced every quarter. Hold SPY only while it is above its 200-day average, with a 15% stop loss. Hold the bonds only while TLT is above its 100-day average, with an 8% stop. Cash earns 4%.
strategy:
name: 60/40 with trend filters
universe: SPY 60%, TLT 40%
from: 2010-01-01
rebalance: quarterly
cash rate: 4%
stop loss: 15%

buy when close > sma(200)
sell when close < sma(200)

for TLT:
  buy when close > sma(100)
  sell when close < sma(100)
  stop loss: 8%

title: QQQ RSI pullback
description: Buy QQQ on sharp dips in an uptrend: RSI(2) under 10 while the price is above its 200-day average. Sell when RSI(2) goes over 70 or after 10 days. 5% stop loss, 5 bps costs, from 2005.
strategy:
name: QQQ RSI pullback
universe: QQQ
from: 2005-01-01
costs: 5 bps
stop loss: 5%

buy when rsi(2) < 10 and close > sma(200)
sell when rsi(2) > 70 or bars held >= 10

title: Momentum rotation
description: Every month, hold the 3 strongest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, TLT and GLD by 6-month momentum, but only those above their 200-day average. Otherwise stay in cash.
strategy:
name: Momentum rotation
universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, TLT, GLD
rebalance: monthly
hold: top 3 by roc(126)

buy when close > sma(200)
sell when close < sma(200)
notes: Six months is about 126 trading days, so the ranking uses roc(126).

title: QQQ moving-average crossover
description: Moving-average crossover on QQQ: buy when the fast average is above the slow one, sell when it is below. I want to try fast from 20 to 100 and slow from 100 to 250. Judge it on data from 2018.
strategy:
name: QQQ moving-average crossover
universe: QQQ
test from: 2018-01-01

fast = 50 in 20..100 step 10
slow = 200 in 100..250 step 50

buy when sma(fast) > sma(slow)
sell when sma(fast) < sma(slow)
notes: You gave ranges but no starting values, so I started fast at 50 and slow at 200.

title: SPY short at 2x below its 50-day average
description: Short the S&P 500 with 2x leverage when it breaks below its 50-day average, and hedge with put options.
strategy:
name: SPY short at 2x below its 50-day average
universe: SPY 200%

short when close < sma(50)
cover when close > sma(50)
notes: Options are not supported, so there is no put hedge: this is the short alone.
The description does not say when to cover, so the short is bought back when SPY closes above its 50-day average again.
SPY stands in for the S&P 500, and its weight of 200% sells short twice the equity.

title: SPY golden cross
description: Buy SPY when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average and sell when it crosses back below. Count 5 bps for each trade.
strategy:
name: SPY golden cross
universe: SPY
costs: 5 bps

buy when sma(50) crosses above sma(200)
sell when sma(50) crosses below sma(200)

title: QQQ confirmed uptrend
description: Only buy QQQ once it has been above its 200-day average for 5 days in a row, and sell after 3 straight days below it. I want fewer false signals than a plain crossover.
strategy:
name: QQQ confirmed uptrend
universe: QQQ

buy when close above sma(200) for 5 bars
sell when close below sma(200) for 3 bars

title: AAPL MACD crossover
description: Trade Apple on MACD crossovers. Start with 10k and a 1 dollar commission on every order.
strategy:
name: AAPL MACD crossover
universe: AAPL
capital: 10k
commission: 1

buy when macd() crosses above macd_signal()
sell when macd() crosses below macd_signal()
notes: You gave no MACD periods, so macd() and macd_signal() use their usual 12, 26 and 9.

title: MSFT strong uptrend
description: Microsoft, strong uptrends only: ADX above 25, +DI above -DI and Aroon up above 70. Get out when the trend is no longer strong or Aroon down passes Aroon up.
strategy:
name: MSFT strong uptrend
universe: MSFT

trending = adx(14) > 25

buy when trending
  and plus_di(14) > minus_di(14)
  and aroon_up(25) > 70
sell when not trending or aroon_down(25) > aroon_up(25)
notes: You gave no lengths, so ADX and the DI lines use 14 bars and Aroon uses 25.

title: QQQ supertrend with parabolic SAR
description: On QQQ I want the supertrend and the parabolic SAR to agree: buy when the supertrend points up and the price is above the SAR, and sell when the price falls under either line.
strategy:
name: QQQ supertrend with parabolic SAR
universe: QQQ

buy when supertrend_up(10, 3) and close > psar(0.02, 0.2)
sell when close < supertrend(10, 3) or close < psar(0.02, 0.2)
notes: You gave no numbers, so the supertrend uses 10 bars and a multiple of 3, and the SAR its usual step of 0.02 and maximum of 0.2.

title: SPY TEMA and DEMA crossover
description: A moving-average crossover on SPY with less lag: the 10-day triple exponential average against the 30-day double exponential average.
strategy:
name: SPY TEMA and DEMA crossover
universe: SPY

buy when tema(10) crosses above dema(30)
sell when tema(10) crosses below dema(30)
notes: You did not say which way to trade it, so it buys when the faster average crosses above the slower one and sells when it crosses back below.

title: SPY adaptive average
description: Use Kaufman's adaptive moving average on the S&P 500: be in while the price is above it and the market is trending rather than choppy.
strategy:
name: SPY adaptive average
universe: SPY

buy when close > kama(10, 2, 30) and efficiency(10) > 0.3
sell when close < kama(10, 2, 30)
notes: SPY stands in for the S&P 500.
KAMA uses its usual 10, 2 and 30, and trending means an efficiency ratio over 0.3.
You did not say when to sell, so it sells when the price falls under the average.

title: SPY regression trend
description: Buy SPY when its 90-day trend is clean: the log-price regression line rises faster than 15% a year, it fits well (R-squared above 0.7) and the price is above the line. Sell when the trend turns down.
strategy:
name: SPY regression trend
universe: SPY

annual = exp(slope(log(close), 90) * 252) - 1

buy when annual > 15% and rsquared(log(close), 90) > 0.7 and log(close) > linreg(log(close), 90)
sell when annual < 0
notes: A year is taken as 252 trading days.

title: QQQ 20-day breakout
description: Turtle-style breakout on QQQ: buy a new 20-day high, sell a new 10-day low. Test 2010 through 2024, and fill at the next day's open.
strategy:
name: QQQ 20-day breakout
universe: QQQ
from: 2010-01-01
to: 2024-12-31
fill: next open

buy when close > highest(20)[1]
sell when close < lowest(10)[1]

title: SPY squeeze breakout
description: Volatility squeeze on SPY: when the Bollinger bands have sat inside the Keltner channel in the last few days and the price then breaks above the channel, buy. Sell when it closes under its 20-day exponential average.
strategy:
name: SPY squeeze breakout
universe: SPY

squeeze = bb_upper(20, 2) < keltner_upper(20, 1.5, 10) and bb_lower(20, 2) > keltner_lower(20, 1.5, 10)

buy when squeeze within 5 bars and close > keltner_upper(20, 1.5, 10)
sell when close < ema(20)
notes: "The last few days" is taken as 5 bars.
The bands use 20 bars and 2 deviations and the channel 20 bars, 1.5 average true ranges and 10 bars, the usual squeeze settings.

title: NVDA breakout with volume
description: Buy NVDA breakouts only when volume agrees: a new 50-day high, the money flow index over 60 and on-balance volume above its 20-day average. Sell when it closes under the 20-day volume-weighted average or Chaikin money flow goes negative.
strategy:
name: NVDA breakout with volume
universe: NVDA

buy when close > highest(50)[1] and mfi(14) > 60 and obv() > sma(obv(), 20)
sell when close < vwap(20) or cmf(20) < 0
notes: You gave no lengths for the money flow index and Chaikin money flow, so they use 14 and 20 bars.

title: NVDA momentum with ATR stops
description: Momentum on NVDA: buy when the 60-day gain is over 15%, the price is above its 50-day exponential average and annualized volatility is under 40%. Stop loss 2 ATR, trailing stop 3 ATR, take profit 6 ATR. Sell if the 60-day gain turns negative.
strategy:
name: NVDA momentum with ATR stops
universe: NVDA
stop loss: 2 atr(14)
trailing stop: 3 atr(14)
take profit: 6 atr(14)

buy when roc(60) > 15% and close > ema(50) and stdev(roc(1), 20) * sqrt(252) < 40%
sell when roc(60) < 0
notes: No ATR length was given, so the stops use 14 bars.
Annualized volatility is the standard deviation of daily returns over 20 bars times the square root of 252.

title: GLD RSI bounce
description: Buy gold (GLD) when the 14-day RSI drops under a level I can tune from 20 to 40, with a stop loss I can tune from 4% to 12%. Sell the first time RSI(14) crosses 50. Judge it on data from 2018.
strategy:
name: GLD RSI bounce
universe: GLD
test from: 2018-01-01
stop loss: stop_pct

limit = 30 in 20..40 step 5
stop_pct = 8% in 4%..12% step 2%

buy when rsi(14) < limit
sell when rsi(14) crosses 50
notes: You gave ranges but no starting values, so I started the RSI level at 30 and the stop at 8%.

title: SPY Bollinger dip
description: Buy SPY when it closes below the lower Bollinger band but is still above its 100-day weighted moving average. Sell when it gets back up to its 20-day median.
strategy:
name: SPY Bollinger dip
universe: SPY

buy when close < bb_lower(20, 2) and close > wma(100)
sell when close > median(20)
notes: The band uses the usual 20 bars and 2 standard deviations.

title: SPY Connors RSI
description: Connors RSI idea on SPY: average RSI(3), the 2-day RSI of the up and down streak, and the percent rank of today's return over 100 days. Buy when that average is under 10 and the price is above its 200-day average, sell when it closes above its 5-day average.
strategy:
name: SPY Connors RSI
universe: SPY

buy when (rsi(3) + rsi(streak(), 2) + percent_rank(roc(1), 100)) / 3 < 10 and close > sma(200)
sell when close > sma(5)

title: SPY three-day slide
description: Buy SPY after a three-day slide of more than 4% while it is above its 200-day average. Sell once it has bounced 5% off its low since I bought, or after 5 days. 5% stop loss.
strategy:
name: SPY three-day slide
universe: SPY
stop loss: 5%

buy when sum(roc(1), 3) < -4% and close > sma(200)
sell when close > lowest since entry * 1.05 or bars held >= 5
notes: The slide is the sum of the last three daily returns.

title: XLP CCI and Williams %R
description: Buy XLP when CCI(20) is under -100 and Williams %R(14) is under -80, as long as it holds above its 100-day average. Sell when CCI is back over 0 or Williams %R rises above -20.
strategy:
name: XLP CCI and Williams %R
universe: XLP

buy when cci(20) < -100 and williams_r(14) < -80 and close > sma(100)
sell when cci(20) > 0 or williams_r(14) > -20

title: SPY pullback to the 50-day average
description: In an uptrend (50-day average above the 200-day), buy SPY on a pullback: the price within one average true range of the 50-day average, the stochastic %K crossing above %D, and RSI(14) between 40 and 50. Sell if it closes under the 200-day average.
strategy:
name: SPY pullback to the 50-day average
universe: SPY

distance = abs(close - sma(50))

buy when sma(50) > sma(200)
  and distance < atr(14)
  and stoch_k(14, 3) crosses above stoch_d(14, 3, 3)
  and rsi(14) between 40 and 50
sell when close < sma(200)
notes: The stochastic uses its usual 14, 3 and 3.
You gave no length for the average true range, so it uses 14 bars.

title: SPY dip after a fresh breakout
description: Buy a quick dip right after a breakout: SPY is above its 200-day average, crossed above it less than 30 days ago, and RSI(2) was under 10 at some point in the last 3 days. Sell when it falls back under the 200-day average.
strategy:
name: SPY dip after a fresh breakout
universe: SPY

buy when close > sma(200) and bars_since(close crosses above sma(200)) < 30 and rsi(2) < 10 within 3 bars
sell when close < sma(200)

title: SPY momentum with steady days
description: Time-series momentum on SPY: be in when the price is above where it was some months ago, but only if at least 6 of the last 10 days were up days. I want to try lookbacks from 3 to 12 months.
strategy:
name: SPY momentum with steady days
universe: SPY

lookback = 126 in 63..252 step 21

buy when close > close[lookback] and count(close > close[1], 10) >= 6
sell when close < close[lookback]
notes: Three to twelve months is 63 to 252 trading days in steps of a month (21 days), and I started at 6 months (126).

title: SPY with VIX and correlation filters
description: Hold SPY while it is above its 200-day average, the VIX is under 25, and SPY and the VIX are still moving against each other (correlation under -0.5 over the last 30 days). Leave when SPY loses its 200-day average or the VIX goes over 30.
strategy:
name: SPY with VIX and correlation filters
universe: SPY

buy when close > sma(200)
  and close of ^VIX < 25
  and correl(close of ^VIX, 30) < -0.5
sell when close < sma(200) or close of ^VIX > 30

title: QQQ dips in a SPY uptrend
description: Buy QQQ dips (3-day RSI under 20) only when both QQQ and SPY are above their 200-day averages. Get out when SPY loses its 200-day average, or when QQQ has closed under its own average two days running.
strategy:
name: QQQ dips in a SPY uptrend
universe: QQQ

uptrend = close > sma(200)

buy when uptrend and uptrend of SPY and rsi(3) < 20
sell when uptrend of SPY == false or (not uptrend and not uptrend[1])

title: SPY RSI(2) by regime
description: Buy SPY on RSI(2) dips, but be pickier in a downtrend: RSI(2) under 15 while it is above its 200-day average, under 5 while it is below. Sell when RSI(2) is over 70.
strategy:
name: SPY RSI(2) by regime
universe: SPY

buy when rsi(2) < if(close > sma(200), 15, 5)
sell when rsi(2) > 70

title: QQQ buffer between two averages
description: Buy QQQ only when it is above both its 50-day and its 200-day average, and sell only when it is below both, so there is a buffer in between.
strategy:
name: QQQ buffer between two averages
universe: QQQ

buy when close > max(sma(50), sma(200))
sell when close < min(sma(50), sma(200))

title: SPY pyramid in three entries
description: Build a SPY position in three steps: buy a third when it's above its 200-day average and RSI(14) is under 50. Add the second third when the price is 2% above my last purchase and the last third when it's 4% above that one. Sell everything if it falls 8% below my average cost.
strategy:
name: SPY pyramid in three entries
universe: SPY
entries: 3

buy when close > sma(200) and rsi(14) < 50
add when close > last entry price * (1 + 0.02 * entries made)
sell when close < entry price * 0.92
notes: Your average cost is entry price, which is the average of the entries made so far.

title: SPY entry with three exits
description: Buy SPY when it crosses above its 20-day average while it's above its 200-day average. Sell when I'm up 20%, after 30 days, or when the price falls 3 average true ranges (22-day) below the highest price since I bought.
strategy:
name: SPY entry with three exits
universe: SPY

buy when close > sma(200) and close crosses above sma(20)
sell when position return > 20% or bars held > 30 or close < highest since entry - 3 * atr(22)

title: BTC hourly Hull trend
description: Bitcoin on Binance hourly bars since the start of 2024: buy when the 24-hour Hull average is rising and the price is above the 200-hour weighted average, sell when the Hull average turns down. Costs 10 bps and slippage 5 bps.
strategy:
name: BTC hourly Hull trend
data: binance
universe: BTCUSDT
interval: 1h
from: 2024-01-01
costs: 10 bps
slippage: 5 bps

buy when hma(24) > hma(24)[1] and close > wma(200)
sell when hma(24) < hma(24)[1]
notes: BTCUSDT is Binance's Bitcoin pair.

title: ETH 15-minute dips
description: Scalp Ether on 15-minute Binance bars through 2025: buy when RSI(14) drops under 30 and sell when it is over 60, with a 1% stop and a 2% target.
strategy:
name: ETH 15-minute dips
data: binance
universe: ETHUSDT
interval: 15m
from: 2025-01-01
to: 2025-12-31
stop loss: 1%
take profit: 2%

buy when rsi(14) < 30
sell when rsi(14) > 60
notes: ETHUSDT is Binance's Ether pair, and through 2025 is read as 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31.

title: BTC daily trend with hourly stops
description: Bitcoin daily trend from Binance: buy above the 50-day average, sell below it, with an 8% stop and a 20% target. A daily bar can reach both, so look at the hourly bars to see which came first.
strategy:
name: BTC daily trend with hourly stops
data: binance
universe: BTCUSDT
interval: 1d
magnify: 1h
stop loss: 8%
take profit: 20%

buy when close > sma(50)
sell when close < sma(50)

title: QQQ 30-week trend

data: yahoo
universe: QQQ
interval: 1w

buy when close > sma(30)
sell when close < sma(30)

title: AAPL gap up on heavy volume
description: Buy Apple the day after it beats earnings estimates and sell a week later.
strategy:
name: AAPL gap up on heavy volume
universe: AAPL

buy when open > close[1] * 1.03 and close > (high + low) / 2 and zscore(volume, 20) > 2
sell when bars held >= 5
notes: Earnings dates and estimates are not available, so a gap up of more than 3% that holds above the middle of the day on unusually heavy volume stands in for a beat.
Unusually heavy volume is more than 2 standard deviations above its 20-day average.
A week is taken as 5 trading days.

title: SPY buy and hold
description: Own SPY and sell a covered call against it every month for income.
strategy:
name: SPY buy and hold
universe: SPY

buy when true
notes: Options are not supported, so no calls are sold: this is the SPY shares alone, bought on the first day and held.

title: SPY RSI swings
description: Trade SPY on 5-minute bars: buy when RSI(14) goes under 30 and sell when it's over 70.
strategy:
name: SPY RSI swings
universe: SPY

buy when rsi(14) < 30
sell when rsi(14) > 70
notes: Yahoo has no intraday bars for stocks, so the 5-minute interval is left out and the rules read daily bars.

title: QQQ trend with target and trailing stop
description: Buy QQQ while it's above its 200-day average. Sell half when I'm up 10% and the rest if it falls 5% from its high.
strategy:
name: QQQ trend with target and trailing stop
universe: QQQ
trailing stop: 5%
take profit: 10%

buy when close > sma(200)
notes: A sale always closes the whole position, so the 10% take profit sells all of it rather than half.

title: SPY Halloween effect
description: Sell in May: buy SPY at the end of October and sell it at the end of April.
strategy:
name: SPY Halloween effect
universe: SPY
fill: close

buy when month == 10 and month_end
sell when month == 4 and month_end
notes: fill: close trades at the closing price of those last days of the month, as your wording suggests, rather than at the next open.

title: SPY turn of the month
description: I've read that stocks do best around the turn of the month. Be in SPY for the last few days of each month and the first few of the next.
strategy:
name: SPY turn of the month
universe: SPY

buy when trading_days_left == 3
sell when trading_day == 3
notes: "The last few days" is taken as the last 3 trading days of the month and "the first few" as the first 3 of the next.

title: SPY turnaround Tuesday
description: Buy SPY at Monday's close when it fell more than 1% that day, and sell at Tuesday's close.
strategy:
name: SPY turnaround Tuesday
universe: SPY
fill: close

buy when weekday == 1 and roc(1) < -1%
sell when weekday == 2
notes: fill: close makes both trades at those closes instead of the next open.

title: QQQ weekend hold
description: Hold QQQ over the weekend only: buy at the last close of each week when it is above its 50-day average, and sell at the first close of the next week.
strategy:
name: QQQ weekend hold
universe: QQQ
fill: close

buy when week_end and close > sma(50)
sell when week_start
notes: fill: close trades at the closes you named instead of the next open.

title: SPY payday window
description: Buy SPY from the 25th of the month and hold it into the first trading day of the next month.
strategy:
name: SPY payday window
universe: SPY

buy when day >= 25
sell when month_start
notes: If the 25th is not a trading day, the buy comes on the next one.

title: SPY first and fourth quarters
description: I only want to be invested in the first and fourth quarters: in from the first day of the year to the end of March, and from the first day of October to the end of the year.
strategy:
name: SPY first and fourth quarters
universe: SPY

buy when year_start or (quarter_start and quarter == 4)
sell when (quarter_end and quarter == 1) or year_end

description: Buy and hold SPY, but I want to be in cash for all of 2022.
strategy:

universe: SPY

buy when year != 2022
sell when year == 2022

title: Blended momentum, top 4
description: Each month, hold the 4 strongest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM, TLT, IEF and GLD. Score each one by averaging its 3, 6 and 12 month returns, and skip anything whose score is negative.

buy when score > 0

notes: A month is about 21 trading days, so 3, 6 and 12 months are roc(63), roc(126) and roc(252).

title: Weekly momentum, top 3
description: Use weekly bars. From SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA and EEM hold the 3 with the best 26-week return, but only those above their 40-week average. Pick again every month, and judge the results from 2018 on.

test from: 2018-01-01
rebalance: monthly
hold: top 3 by roc(26)

buy when close > sma(40)
sell when close < sma(40)

title: Calm funds get more weight

strategy:

buy when true

description: Breakout system on SPY, QQQ, IWM and EFA: buy a close above the previous 100-day high, sell below the previous 50-day low. Risk 1% of the account on each trade, with a stop 2 ATRs away.
strategy:
name: Breakouts sized by risk

risk per trade: 1% at 2 atr(14)

buy when close > highest(100)[1]
sell when close < lowest(50)[1]

title: Fast stocks, slow havens
description: SPY, QQQ, TLT and GLD, reset each month. The stock funds buy above their 50-day average, the bonds and gold above their 200-day, and each sells when it closes back under its own average. Add a 12% trailing stop on the stock funds only.

buy when close > sma(200)
sell when close < sma(200)

for SPY, QQQ:
  buy when close > sma(50)
  sell when close < sma(50)
  trailing stop: 12%

title: One early entry, a shared exit
description: SPY, QQQ, IWM and EFA. Buy each above its 200-day average, except QQQ, which I want in earlier on the 50-day. Everything sells under the 200-day, and all four get a 10% stop loss.
strategy:
name: One early entry, a shared exit
universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA

buy when close > sma(200)

for QQQ:
  buy when close > sma(50)

for all:
  sell when close < sma(200)
  stop loss: 10%

title: A stop for each fund
description: Hold SPY 40%, TLT 30% and GLD 30%, each only above its 150-day average, rebalanced every quarter. Stops: a 10% stop loss on SPY, 6% on TLT, and on gold an 8% trailing stop with a 30% take profit.
strategy:
name: A stop for each fund
universe: SPY 40%, TLT 30%, GLD 30%
rebalance: quarterly

buy when close > sma(150)
sell when close < sma(150)

for SPY:
  stop loss: 10%

for TLT:
  stop loss: 6%

for GLD:
  trailing stop: 8%
  take profit: 30%

title: Sectors with a market filter
description: Buy XLK, XLV, XLF and XLE when they're above their 100-day average, but only while SPY is above its 200-day. Sell a fund under its 100-day, or all of them if SPY drops under its 200-day.
strategy:
name: Sectors with a market filter
universe: XLK, XLV, XLF, XLE

market_up = close of SPY > sma(200) of SPY

buy when close > sma(100) and market_up
sell when close < sma(100) or not market_up

title: Stocks while the curve is normal
description: Hold half SPY and half QQQ while the 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread is above zero and the fund is above its 200-day average. Get out when the curve inverts or the trend breaks. Cash earns the 3-month T-bill rate.
strategy:
name: Stocks while the curve is normal
universe: SPY 50%, QQQ 50%
cash rate: fred:DGS3MO

curve_ok = close of fred:T10Y2Y > 0

buy when curve_ok and close > sma(200)
sell when not curve_ok or close < sma(200)
notes: I used FRED's T10Y2Y for the spread and DGS3MO for the 3-month bill yield.

title: SPY unless unemployment rises
description: Stay in SPY unless unemployment is rising.
strategy:
name: SPY unless unemployment rises
symbol: SPY

jobless_rising = close of fred:UNRATE > sma(close, 12) of fred:UNRATE

buy when not jobless_rising
sell when jobless_rising
notes: I read "rising" as the unemployment rate (FRED series UNRATE) being above its 12-month average.
UNRATE has one reading a month, so its average covers the last 12 readings.

title: BTC and ETH trend
description: BTC and ETH from Binance, 60/40, daily bars: hold each while it's above its 100-day average. Costs are 10 bps.
strategy:
name: BTC and ETH trend
data: binance
universe: BTCUSDT 60%, ETHUSDT 40%
interval: 1d
costs: 10 bps

buy when close > sma(100)
sell when close < sma(100)
notes: Binance quotes in USDT, so BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT stand for bitcoin and ether.

title: Trend on Tiingo prices
description: Use my Tiingo key for the prices. SPY, QQQ and IWM, in the market above the 200-day average and out below it.
strategy:
name: Trend on Tiingo prices
data: tiingo
universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM

buy when close > sma(200)
sell when close < sma(200)

title: Tiingo stock, Yahoo bonds and bitcoin
description: Take SPY from Tiingo and the rest from Yahoo (say Yahoo outright). 70% SPY, 20% TLT, 10% bitcoin, put back to those weights each year.
strategy:
name: Tiingo stock, Yahoo bonds and bitcoin
data: yahoo
universe: tiingo:SPY 70%, TLT 20%, BTC-USD 10%
rebalance: yearly

buy when true
notes: Yahoo spells bitcoin BTC-USD.

title: SPY and my gold file
description: My vault has Data/gold.csv with gold prices. Hold half in that file and half in SPY, each only while above its 100-day average.
strategy:
name: SPY and my gold file
universe: SPY 50%, csv:Data/gold.csv 50%

buy when close > sma(100)
sell when close < sma(100)

title: Stocks on my risk score
description: My file Data/regime.csv has a daily column called risk_on, between 0 and 1. Keep 70% in SPY while it's above 0.5 and sell when it drops below 0.5. The other 30% sits in TLT all the time.
strategy:
name: Stocks on my risk score
universe: SPY 70%, TLT 30%

for SPY:
  buy when column(risk_on) of csv:Data/regime.csv > 0.5
  sell when column(risk_on) of regime < 0.5

for TLT:
  buy when true

title: Top 2 by my own score
description: I scored three funds myself and saved each as a CSV with prices and a score column: Data/spy_scored.csv, Data/efa_scored.csv and Data/eem_scored.csv. Each month hold the two with the highest score.
strategy:
name: Top 2 by my own score
universe: csv:Data/spy_scored.csv, csv:Data/efa_scored.csv, csv:Data/eem_scored.csv
rebalance: monthly
hold: top 2 by column(score)

title: Long above, short below the 200-day
description: SPY and QQQ: long above the 200-day average, short below it, flipping each way.
strategy:
name: Long above, short below the 200-day
universe: SPY, QQQ

buy when close > sma(200)
short when close < sma(200)
notes: You gave no weights, so each fund gets half the equity, long or short.

title: Large caps long, small caps short
description: Be long SPY while it's above its 100-day average and short IWM while it's under its own 100-day, half the account each.
strategy:
name: Large caps long, small caps short
universe: SPY 50%, IWM 50%

for SPY:
  buy when close > sma(100)
  sell when close < sma(100)

for IWM:
  short when close < sma(100)
  cover when close > sma(100)

title: Short the weak sectors
description: Short JETS and KRE when each is under its 100-day average and buy them back once they close over their 50-day. My broker charges 2% a year to borrow.
strategy:
name: Short the weak sectors
universe: JETS, KRE
borrow fee: 2%

short when close < sma(100)
cover when close > sma(50)
notes: You gave no weights, so each fund is sold short for half the equity.

title: Leveraged 60/40
description: Run a 60/40 at 2x: 120% SPY and 80% TLT, reset every quarter. Margin costs me 5% a year.
strategy:
name: Leveraged 60/40
universe: SPY 120%, TLT 80%
rebalance: quarterly
margin rate: 5%

buy when true

title: Trend at 1.5x
description: Trend following on a few index funds, with a bit of leverage.
strategy:
name: Trend at 1.5x
universe: SPY, QQQ, EFA
size: 150%

buy when close > sma(150)
sell when close < sma(150)
notes: You named no funds, so I used SPY, QQQ and EFA.
I read "a bit of leverage" as 150% of the equity, shared equally between the funds.
You gave no trend length, so each fund is held while above its 150-day average.

title: Build in thirds
description: SPY and QQQ, half each. Buy a first third of the position above the 100-day average, add another third each time the price is 3% over my last purchase, up to three. Sell under the 100-day average.
strategy:
name: Build in thirds
universe: SPY 50%, QQQ 50%
entries: 3

buy when close > sma(100)
add when close > last entry price * 1.03
sell when close < sma(100)

title: SPY and QQQ held, no options
description: Hold SPY and QQQ and write monthly covered calls on both to collect the premium.
strategy:
name: SPY and QQQ held, no options
universe: SPY, QQQ

buy when true
notes: Options are not supported, so there are no covered calls: this only holds the two funds, half each.

title: Oil and gold ETFs for futures
description: Trend-follow crude oil and gold futures: long when the market is trending up and flat otherwise.
strategy:
name: Oil and gold ETFs for futures
universe: USO, GLD

buy when close > sma(100)
sell when close < sma(100)
notes: Futures are not supported, so USO and GLD, two ETFs that follow oil and gold, stand in.
You gave no trend length, so I used the 100-day average.

title: Seven large stocks, no P/E screen
description: Buy the 5 cheapest of AAPL, MSFT, JPM, XOM, JNJ, PG and KO by P/E ratio, rebalanced every quarter.
strategy:
name: Seven large stocks, no P/E screen
universe: AAPL, MSFT, JPM, XOM, JNJ, PG, KO
rebalance: quarterly

buy when true
notes: The language has no earnings or valuation data, so there is no P/E ranking.
This holds all seven equally and resets them each quarter. Narrow the list to your five cheapest by hand if you want only those.

title: Momentum, long leg only
description: Each month go long the 3 strongest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM, TLT, GLD and DBC by 6-month momentum, and short the 3 weakest.
strategy:
name: Momentum, long leg only
universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM, TLT, GLD, DBC
rebalance: monthly
hold: top 3 by roc(126)
notes: A ranking cannot go short, so the 3 weakest are not sold short: this holds the top 3 only.
Six months is about 126 trading days, so the ranking uses roc(126).
